title: Cardinal Billing Account Purpose Rate on Representative Payment Fees: Questions Answered
content:
**Rule.** A purpose rate multiplies the representative payment fee on a Cardinal Billing Account assisted payment: **0.50** when a renewal down payment invoice (installment 1 of a term) was posted on the account no more than 5 calendar days before the payment date; **0.75** when no such invoice was posted in that span but an additional-premium bill was; **1.00** otherwise.

## Questions answered

**How is the 5-day span counted?**
In calendar days from the posting date of the invoice or bill to the payment date. An invoice posted on the payment date itself, or 1 to 5 calendar days before it, is within the span; one posted 6 calendar days before it is not.

**Which entries count as a renewal down payment invoice?**
An installment 1 invoice of a term posted on the account's billing history; the latest such invoice is the one read.

**Which entries count as an additional-premium bill?**
An additional-premium bill posted on the account's billing history; the latest such bill is the one read.

**Both an installment 1 invoice and an additional-premium bill were posted within the span. Which rate applies?**
0.50. The 0.75 rate applies only when no installment 1 invoice was posted in the span.

| Installment 1 invoice posted within 5 calendar days | Additional-premium bill posted within 5 calendar days | Purpose rate |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes or No | 0.50 |
| No | Yes | 0.75 |
| No | No | 1.00 |

**Hypothetical figure.** A representative fee figured at $3.50, with an installment 1 invoice posted 2 days before the payment date, is multiplied by 0.50.
